findings.section: Behaviour contract / C2 and Decided here (C2 applies to the words after every wrapper)
findings.summary: C2 says an expanded word may be any text, including several words, but it only matches the words after the wrappers. A word a wrapper skips (an option, timeout's duration, exec -a's name, an env NAME=value) can expand to the command's name. That bypass gets through today and still gets through after B35.
findings.evidence: Today's binary, review phase: `command -$x push` -> allow, `nice -n$N push` -> allow, `timeout $T push` -> allow, `exec -a $x push origin` -> allow. With T='5 git', `timeout $T push` runs `timeout 5 git push`. Likewise `env A=$x push` with x='1 git'. internal/fence/judge.go skipDashes/skipNice/skipTimeout/skipExec/skipEnv drop these words before `match` sees them, and the C2 contract and 'Decided here' never bring them back.
findings.fix: Add to C2: a word that a wrapper skips and that is expanded (an unquoted or double-quoted `$`, a glob or a brace) may hold the command's name, so the command is refused with C2's own `command word <word> expands and cannot be judged`. Add `review  timeout $T push   → deny: command word $T expands and cannot be judged` to the worked example and the failures it must catch. C3's line `command -$v git push` then changes to that answer too (`-$v` is skipped by `command`), or keep it by excluding that word explicitly. State which one.

findings.section: Why this shape / Subshells, not only braces
findings.summary: The brief says B26's run counted one subshell. B26's run recorded none. The subshell denials were in B22.0 and B24, as the executive summary itself says.
findings.evidence: docs/design-notes/copilot-cli-experiments.md:433 (B26): '5, all shell syntax the hook cannot judge (4 `for`, 1 `$(…)`)'. Line 251 (B22.0) and line 365 (B24) each record 1 subshell. Issue 83 cites B22's acceptance.
findings.fix: Write 'and B22.0's and B24's runs counted one each'.

findings.summary: The brief's figures for the kept sessions (52 calls, 5 holding `$`, and the `command -v curl` denial) rest on a design-note section that is uncommitted. That section credits the `command -v` denial to 'B32's and B33's kept sessions' under the plan fence, not specifically to 'B32's plan session'. (Unsure: the attribution may be right. The session records in the acceptance clones would settle it.)
findings.evidence: `git diff --stat` shows docs/design-notes/copilot-cli-experiments.md modified, +9 lines: '### The shell calls of the kept sessions (for B35, 2026-11-03)'. The section reads: 'one `command -v node; …; command -v curl; vloop version` … (`curl is denied by the plan fence`)'.
findings.fix: Commit the note's new section with the brief's ready merge. Either say 'a plan session of B32's or B33's kept sessions' or add the run to the note.

decisions: Drop the leading keyword and judge the rest; no shell grammar (mvdan.cc/sh rejected). Agree: nothing inside is judged less than one per line.
case, esac, select, function, coproc and [[ stay refused. Agree: none appears among the counted denials.

An expanded word is any text, one or several words, even double-quoted (where no splitting happens). Agree, it fails closed. Costs not named in the brief: in a work session `rm "$f"` and `rm *.tmp` become denied (Bash(rm -rf:*) matches with $f = -rf), and so does `git log "$BASE"..HEAD` (Bash(git log*--output*)). Worth naming next to `git diff "$BASE"`.
Quoted or escaped is literal. `{}`/`@{u}` (no , or .. inside) and a `[` with no `]` after it are not expansions. Agree.
A command name holding a glob or brace is refused with the new message `command word <word> expands and cannot be judged`. Agree.
command -v / -V (with p) run nothing; type, which and hash need nothing. Agree.
Subshells are read; $(, <( and >( stay refused; a word after `)` is refused. Agree.
A keyword after a wrapper is not dropped (`env ! x` stays `shell syntax ! cannot be judged`). Agree; this is today's answer, verified.
C2 applies in every phase, including plan and review-brief. Agree.
The C4 wording for configuration.md, fence-audit.md and fence check's help. No opinion; the anchor sentences exist verbatim.
